benchmark_evidence.observed: Explicit sharing of private drafts, inbox/conversation-based access, single-editor takeover and live editing visibility are documented. Foundly does not yet claim live co-editing or inbox access equivalence.

The documented draft-reply API uses drafts write scope and explicit conversation/channel references, private/shared modes, recipient lists and bounded attachments. This is benchmark evidence, not a Foundly implementation claim.

Front documents sender-only reply, reply-all and forwarding in existing or new conversations. Foundly currently proves internal source-bound draft preparation only, not these complete delivery/threading workflows.

capabilities.foundly_current: Owned drafts, templates, threads and preferences remain standalone. Draft sharing uses explicit owner/admin authority, a bounded tenant member search, current member status and current parent ACL for all retained revisions. Edits use revision preconditions. Restore creates a new draft revision, preserves current collaborators, binds idempotency to the actor/input and does not send. History survives encrypted restart and persistence failure rolls back draft, history, audit and receipt together. Legacy unversioned drafts retain a labelled baseline. Dashboard separates drafts from retained messages and treats unavailable, invalid or incomplete source contracts as unavailable. A 20,000-revision fixture resolves current parent ACL once per read/export, with no cross-request authorization cache. Production client handlers preserve revision preconditions across paginated history and do not redraw detached workspaces; simulated DOM tests do not establish browser acceptance. Reply/forward preparation now binds the exact retained message revision/hash, validates explicit recipients, creates only an unsent internal draft and never copies external source instructions into its body. Current source ownership/capabilities govern derived drafts and revision history; retained export still survives module disablement under the existing export permission and current source ownership. Drafts now retain bounded UTF-8 .txt attachments with exact byte hashes, private encrypted content storage, current parent/source ACL, CAS attach/detach, immutable historical references and restore, and owned export after module disablement. Attachment bytes are excluded from generic Data and ZERO projections; native client downloads validate the hash and use text/plain without inline rendering. No malware scan is claimed. A dedicated retained-message inbox now searches subject/body/participants with pagination, direction and personal read/archive filters. Unknown personal read state and external mailbox completeness remain explicit; changed source revisions invalidate old read evidence. Personal state is isolated per current user, revision-bound, audited, atomic and exportable under current source access. Native message detail is read-only, with separate draft preparation; opening a message never silently records it as read. Real sessions prove body-wait source changes/reownership, readonly denial and encrypted replay. Client handlers reject late search results and detached updates. Explicit read-only IMAP INBOX receipt now uses verified implicit TLS on 993, pinned public IPv4, AUTH PLAIN, EXAMINE and BODY.PEEK. Bounded UIDVALIDITY/UID scans retain exact encrypted MIME bytes with integrity-checked current-source downloads and owned export. Provider Draft flags never create internal drafts or count as recorded messages; later observed draft flags hide ordinary inbox/messages/snapshot and derived-source reads while labelled historical owned export remains. Missing/oversized/malformed content stays unavailable. Pagination, changed UID sets, atomic import rollback and current account/member revocation pass local TLS, unit, real HTTP/restart and production-handler fixtures. Scan coverage describes observed UIDs over a window, including excluded drafts; it is not a current external message count, identity proof or delivery receipt. No real provider account was accessed. Source-bound reply review now includes exact RFC 5322 In-Reply-To/References headers; source revision changes block review and submission. Approved submission persists the same linkage without claiming recipient delivery; forwards do not acquire reply headers. Current-source conversations derive only from visible retained headers, never subject equality, and expose duplicate-ID ambiguity, incomplete participants and unknown external coverage. Native HTTP, isolated approved-submission, encrypted restart and production DOM handlers pass. Malformed Reply-To is unavailable instead of silently selecting a different recipient. Provider Draft flags continue to withdraw ordinary message and derived-draft access. Internal draft comments and replies now use current parent/source access, exact source revisions, author-only withdrawal with retained originals, bounded history, actor/input replay and atomic encrypted persistence. A separate sixty-second editing grant exposes a shared working copy without changing the saved draft or Messages count. Explicit confirmed takeover rotates the private grant and blocks old editors, including an already-authenticated HTTP save awaiting its body. Current membership/source/write permissions and expiry govern each update; tokens stay out of reads, Data, audit and owned exports. Native controls publish work text while editing, retain local text on takeover/conflict, preserve pending confirmation during polling, clear revoked source views and discard detached responses. Unit, real-session/restart and production DOM-handler tests cover these contracts; actual browser/keyboard/viewport and provider acceptance remain unproven. Native and ZERO reply-all preparation now binds the exact current visible source recipients and configured sender. It preserves separate To/Cc, excludes the configured sender and repeated addresses, never copies blind recipients, and returns unavailable when source recipient or sender data is incomplete. Versioned source fingerprints preserve prior reply/forward contracts while binding new Cc and thread metadata. Draft editing, shared work text, immutable revisions/restores, review preview and recorded outbound messages retain Cc. Every To/Cc recipient requires the same current purpose preference and designated exact-source approval; the SMTP envelope includes all approved recipients while MIME preserves their header roles and reply linkage. Isolated approved transport, real native/ZERO HTTP body-wait changes, current-source replay, encrypted restart and production handlers pass; no live provider send or browser acceptance is claimed. PDF, PNG and JPEG attachments now require bounded signature checks and a successful local ClamAV process before atomic attachment. Exact bytes and immutable scan receipts survive history/restore and current-source owned export; binary content stays out of generic Data and downloads as hash-checked octet-stream without inline rendering. Scanner execution uses fixed arguments, no shell, no inherited application credentials, private temporary storage, current authority/configuration checks, official recent database requirements, limits and strict exit/result validation. Alerts, skipped/error/timeout outcomes and source revocation while the process runs never attach a file. Review/submission refuse expired binary scans without deleting the original file/history. Actual subprocess fixtures, real HTTP/restart and production handlers pass; they do not prove a real installed scanner/database, malware detection rate, browser or live-provider acceptance. Legacy text attachments remain explicitly unscanned. The current scratch runtime lacks clamscan; no production dependency was changed. Dedicated Google mail OAuth now uses explicit encrypted email client configuration, one-use member/tenant/configuration-bound state with S256 PKCE, actual granted mail scope/expiry and verified provider subject/email. A fixed inert return page completes through an explicit same-origin authenticated POST, preserving SameSite=Strict sessions and origin checks. Fixed DNS-pinned HTTPS token/userinfo endpoints send secrets only after TLS/peer verification. Current role/configuration/disconnection races, incomplete replacement preservation, encrypted restart/rollback, automatic guarded refresh, stable approved account identity, stale inbox revision rejection before refresh and replay without another provider operation pass isolated TLS, actual HTTP-session and production DOM regressions. Passive reads never exchange tokens. Local disconnection does not revoke Google consent. Private tokens/state are excluded from Data/audit/export; owned metadata is explicit. No real account/provider/browser acceptance or production mutation is claimed. Scanned PDF/PNG/JPEG and newly supported DOCX/XLSX/PPTX now use a 3 MiB per-file, 6 MiB current-draft and 9 MiB MIME bound through the existing encrypted attachment/review/submission path. Bounded ZIP inspection validates stored/deflated/streamed packages, local-central names/flags/sizes/CRC, complete streams and expansion limits while refusing encrypted, macro, duplicate, traversal and unverifiable structures. The existing mandatory scanner uses a versioned bounded policy; V1 receipts remain valid only for their original smaller file/type scope. Actual isolated scanner processes, real-session large-file/Office HTTP upload/download/restart, current source controls and exact greater-than-8-MiB approved MIME regression pass. Inert downloads, private export and unchanged draft/message semantics remain intact. No real malware detection, live provider delivery, Office rendering, browser or production acceptance is claimed; remaining provider/workflow/capability gaps stay open. Owned Communication templates now create internal drafts through explicit literal values and version-bound native or ZERO preview/confirmation. Missing values produce unavailable content, not an apparently complete draft. Actor/tenant/source/input-bound creation, atomic history/audit/receipt, encrypted replay, current template ACL across derived drafts/history/sharing/export and source-free ZERO retention pass unit, real-session body-wait and production DOM contracts. Catalog edits preserve the previously applied draft/version and exact approval; accepted isolated SMTP records retain that origin. Separate designated review, current purpose/account policy and explicit send confirmation remain required. Messages is unchanged by internal draft creation. No live provider/browser acceptance or production mutation is claimed; remaining capability gates stay open.
